messages:
rachel: Quick sync: we're cutting a new base-image rebuild Fri 03:00 UTC. Goal: distroless base, tiny libc, cosign->KMS signing, and SBOM attached. Need signatory RBAC + long-term audit retention confirmed before merge.
lucas: For clarity, current prod signer SA has roles/cloudkms.cryptoSigner and storage.objectViewer. CI runner impersonates signer-sa today. I'm proposing removing iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator from prod. Thoughts?
jon: Removing tokenCreator is good. Alternative: let CI use OIDC + KMS-based key without impersonating signer-sa. That reduces blast radius. We should test IAM flow in staging first.
maya: Compliance asks we capture structured attestations to BigQuery with schema: image_digest, signature_kms_version, signer_principal, build_id, sbom_url, cve_scan_summary. sec-bot, can we get a template?
sec-bot: Template created: https://internal.redwood/templates/attestations/image-sign-v2.json. Fields: [image_digest, signature_kms_version, signer_principal, build_id, sbom_url, cve_scan_summary, cosign_version]
lucas: Small implementation note: cosign with GCP KMS uses a key reference like `gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/rebuild/cryptoKeys/cosign/cryptoKeyVersions/1`. We should record the cryptoKeyVersion in the attestation, not just the key ring.
rachel: How do we handle key rotation? If we roll to v2, older images signed with v1 must still be verifiable. Proposal: add manifest annotation `redwood.com/signing-keyset` listing allowed key versions per image, and have verifier consult that list.
jon: Also add a verifier denylist for compromised key versions. Verifier checks: 1) signature matches one of the key versions in the keyset, 2) key version not in denylist, 3) signature timestamp within validity window.
maya: Retention: legal requires 2 years for image attestations and sign logs. Our KMS logs are 90d. Need retention sink to archive attestation JSON + KMS key-use logs to longterm bucket, TTL=730d. ops-bot, open ticket?
ops-bot: SECG-4899 created: archive attestations + KMS audit logs -> gs://redwood-audit-archive TTL=730d. Owners: eng-infra, security.
lucas: RBAC proposal: view key metadata -> security-readers + SRE-oncall. Sign rights -> CI-signing-runner-sa + small signer-admin group only. No developer direct sign perms. Add conditional binding requiring device-managed + corp IP for signer-admin.
rachel: Add MFA condition for manual sign operators. Also require audit log entry for any `cryptoKeyVersions.*.asymmetricSign` with label `operation=base-image-rebuild`.
jon: For vuln triage: during rebuild we will run SBOM generation + vuln scan stage. If a CVE >= 7.0 appears in base packages, fail the rebuild and escalate. Queue: security-team oncall -> open vuln ticket with triage fields.
maya: Incident playbook for a signing key compromise draft: revoke key version, add version to verifier denylist, re-sign minimal critical images with new key, push verifier canary to 3% traffic, notify customers and compliance, run forensic on key access. I'll attach to rebuild checklist.
rachel: Who will own the re-sign job? lucas? We need an automated re-sign pipeline and manual fallback.
lucas: I can own the automation. Plan: re-sign tool reads list of critical images, pulls SBOM + build_id, signs with new key, writes attestation to GCS and BigQuery, then issues a staged rollout for verifier.
jon: Testing note: in staging we'll simulate a key compromise by adding a fake denylist entry and verifying verifier rejects old signatures. Add test vectors to the pipeline.
maya: Also ensure that SBOM + attestation are signed and stored atomically. If attestation is missing, deployment should fail verification.
rachel: OK: action items: lucas remove tokenCreator in staging and report blockers, lucas create manifest-annotation PR with `redwood.com/signing-keyset`, sam/maya to update attestation schema and retention ticket is open. We'll do tabletop after playbook draft.
sec-bot: Reminder: security weekly sync Thu 16:00 UTC to review rebuild playbook.
lucas: Starting tests now, will post failures here.
